PROJECT SUPPORT

A Clear Brief.
A Better Starting Point.

Find answers about product requirements, samples, files and the information needed to plan your packaging.

Updated October 21, 2026

Minimum quantities depend on the box format, dimensions, paper and finishing method. Tell us your expected quantity so the specification and order requirements can be reviewed together.

The schedule depends on sampling, material availability, finishing and quantity. Confirm the sample approval date, production window and shipping plan in the final quotation.

A physical sample helps confirm product fit, paper feel, opening behavior and print. Agree on sampling scope, cost and timing before proceeding.

Share your logo files, color references and preferred artwork. A physical proof or approved sample should be used as the final production reference.

Foil stamping, embossing, debossing, spot UV, soft-touch lamination and textured papers are possible directions. The appropriate process is confirmed for your chosen material and artwork.

Payment arrangements, sampling charges and production milestones are confirmed in the project quotation. Request a written breakdown before approving an order.

Share the destination, required arrival date and packing requirements. Confirm freight options, responsibilities and any local import requirements with the final shipping plan.

Browse magnetic and lift-off gift boxes, drawers, tubes, bags, specialty shapes, color printed corrugated shipping cartons, printed mailers and white-card folding cartons.

Price depends on size, construction, material, print coverage, finish and quantity. The planning calculator is illustrative; a final quotation uses your confirmed specification.

Paperboard inserts, kraft papers and separable components can be explored. Confirm exact material composition and any environmental claims for your project.

Provide the dimensions and weight of each item. Paperboard, fabric-lined and foam insert directions can then be reviewed for presentation and support.
